name: Musée d'art de Joliette
funding: Quebec ministries, Canada Council and Ville de Joliette. Énergir, Power Corporation, Fondation Hydro-Québec, Caisse Desjardins and the Lassonde and DeSève foundations are among its lead partners (2025 annual report).
watch: UNVERIFIED: Reports page unavailable. Énergir (natural-gas utility) and Fondation Famille Pierre Lassonde (mining fortune) on current partners list; Power Corp funds a named room.
records_note: It posts nine annual reports from 2016-17 to 2024-25 with audited statements, names its board and lists partners and donors.

name: Galerie de l'UQAM
funding: University gallery. Named partners: Canada Council for the Arts, CALQ and UQAM; donations go through the UQAM foundation.
records_note: The gallery posts nothing itself; parent UQAM posts annual reports from 2001-02 with financial results, and the gallery shows three undated partner logos.

name: The Polygon Gallery
funding: Opened 2017 on C$20M campaign; 2024 supporters: Canada Council, BC Arts Council, North Vancouver, BMO ($150k+), TD, RBC, Rogers, Polygon Homes, Audain endowment.
watch: UNVERIFIED: Corporate donors unnamed. Neptune Terminals (Teck/Canpotex coal-and-potash export terminal) and shipbuilder Seaspan ULC give $15k+; Port of Vancouver too.
records_note: Posts annual reports for 2021 to 2024; the 2024 report holds financial statements, a named donor list for 2024 and the board of directors.

name: Musée national des beaux-arts du Québec
funding: C$34.1M revenue 2023-24 (C$24.5M Quebec grants), 248,643 visitors; sponsors Hydro-Québec, Simons, Air Canada, Banque Nationale, BMO, Desjardins, RBC Foundation.
watch: UNVERIFIED: Loto-Québec sponsorship and the Lassonde (mining) pavilion gift not checked. Donor wall lists Imperial Oil ($500k+ cumulative, not in 2023-24 list), Rio Tinto, Osisko, SNC-Lavalin, Loto-Québec; Lassonde (mining) pavilion.
records_note: Posts its 2023-24 and 2024-25 annual reports with audited statements, a named donor list for the 2025-26 campaign, and its board in the reports.

name: Owens Art Gallery
funding: 2023-24 public grants c. CAD 240k (Canada Council $180k, NB Tourism, Heritage & Culture $59k, Town of Sackville $1k) plus Mount Allison University; small private internship donors.
watch: UNVERIFIED: Not researched. Private names on the roster: Heather and Ian Bourne, Jean and Peter Flemington Trust, J.E.A.
records_note: Posts annual reports for 2021-22 to 2025-26 and names internship donors; it has no accounts or board list, as part of Mount Allison University.

name: The Rooms
watch: Cenovus Energy funds the Celebrating Diversity Edukit ($20k 2023-24 and 2024-25); Chevron's 3-year $492k school-programme deal ended June 2025; proposal pitched to BP Canada March 2025.
why_flagged: Cenovus Energy funds the Celebrating Diversity Edukit ($20k 2023-24 and 2024-25); Chevron's 3-year $492k school-programme deal ended June 2025; proposal pitched to BP Canada March 2025.
records_note: The Rooms' annual reports for 2017-18 to 2025-26 sit on the ministry site with audited statements and donor names; its own site lists the board.

name: Art Gallery of Greater Victoria
funding: Revenue c. CAD 6.1M in 2025 (charity filing via Wikidata); BC, City of Victoria, members, AGGV Foundation endowment.
watch: UNVERIFIED: Not researched beyond the site. aggv.ca returns 403 to all fetches; the Wayback copy of the 2023/24 annual report is truncated at 1MB and the 2025/26 report is not archived.
why_flagged: Name to know: TD Bank pleaded guilty in October 2024 to US money-laundering conspiracy and Bank Secrecy Act failures, paying about $3B. Earned and contributed income supplies the other 60 percent. The March 2026 sponsor page lists local firms and TD; no excluded sponsor.
records_note: Its site blocks automated access with a bot check; search listings show an annual report archive, a 2024-25 financial report and a named board page.

name: Winnipeg Art Gallery-Qaumajuq
funding: 2024 donor list: Canada, Manitoba, City of Winnipeg, Nunavut; TD Bank Group ($100-249k), Canada Life, Power Corporation, RBC, Manitoba Liquor & Lotteries, Richardson, Asper Foundation.
records_note: Its site blocks automated access; search results show annual reports from 2014-15 to 2024-25 with a supporter list, summary statements and a named board chair.

name: Museo de Arte Contemporáneo de Santiago
watch: Two sites: Parque Forestal and Quinta Normal.
records_note: Posts none of its own; parent University of Chile posts a 2014-2018 report, budgets and execution reports, and a Consejo Universitario list.

name: Guangdong Times Museum
funding: Backed until 2022 by developer Times China. Reopened March 2024 on a quarter of its budget, with a January 2024 artist auction; no current funder is named.
watch: Curatorial staff fell from 18 to three. The museum says it will seek a range of donors instead of one backer.
records_note: Its Chinese site names its funders (updated 18 May 2026) and staff, but posts no annual report or accounts, and no board of directors.

name: How Art Museum
funding: Private museum of hotelier-collector Zheng Hao, opened 2017 beside his Onehome Art Hotel in Zhangjiang.
watch: Sister venue to his private museum in Wenzhou, opened 2013.
records_note: The museum's official site did not load (howartmuseum.org returned a gateway error), so nothing about its reports, accounts, funders or board could be checked.

name: Power Station of Art
funding: State museum under the Shanghai Municipal Administration of Culture and Tourism; the city paid $64M for the conversion; free entry; 700,000 visitors in 2019.
records_note: The museum's site has no annual report, accounts, sponsor list or board; it names an academic committee, and the city posts only project budgets.
